title: Grill — dynamic model & effort catalog per harness
summary:
Goal (pipeline task): stop hand-adding each new model and its effort ladder release by release; read them from each harness's own CLI, and keep older CLIs working.

**11 decisions** shape the plan, then a **confirm-or-override list** of defaults I'd bet on (one click each). Start with **Scope** and the **Claude** section: they decide most of the plan's shape. The evidence comes from `docs/plans/dynamic-model-catalog-investigation.md` (spikes S1–S6, run on 2026-11-17).

Today a typical "add model X" PR touches **15–26 files**. 11 migrations exist only to normalize or retire model ids.

proven.text: **Claude can report its models and per-model efforts with no quota spent.** `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json` plus one `initialize` control request returns 14 models, each with `value`, `resolvedModel`, `displayName`, `supportedEffortLevels`, `supportsFastMode`. ~1.7 s, no prompt sent, no session dir created. Same list on 2.1.321 and 2.1.326. The effort fields exist since **2.1.49**; older CLIs return ids and labels only.

**codex, fx and opencode are already dynamic, efforts included** (`model/list`, `fx models --json`, opencode v1/v2 probes). OpenCode is the in-repo precedent for "dynamic + older versions": no curated rows, synthesized effort rows for unknown variants.

**Naively wiring claude discovery doubles the picker**: today's merge gives 29–30 rows for 16 curated ones ("Opus 5.5" twice…), because claude reports aliases (`opus`) and full ids (`claude-opus-5`) while agetor uses `opus-5.5`. No test would catch it.
**Every probe failure already degrades to the curated tables** (`mergeModelOptions` rule 2, `supportedEfforts`' curated fallback). Old CLIs keep working as long as curated rows exist.

proven: **Gemini ≥ 0.67** has `gemini models -o json` (ids, labels, context limits, no thinking levels). Older Gemini has no listing, which today's `[]` handles. Web source only: gemini isn't installed here.

Claude's alias rows (`opus`/`sonnet`/`fable`/`haiku` → `resolvedModel`) say which release owns each family. That is exactly what the hand switch `claudeModelPickerFamily` (`src/bun/agents.ts:345`) encodes today, so it can be derived.

sections.title: Scope
sections.intro: What this change covers. These decide the plan's work breakdown.

questions.title: Which harnesses get new or extended discovery in this change?
questions.why: Each ticked harness is a probe + parser + fixtures + tests + doc update. Unticked ones keep today's behavior.
questions.context:
Status per kind today: **claude** none (`discoverClaude` returns `[]`); **cursor** flat `--list-models`, efforts only through the hand-kept `CURSOR_MODEL_SPECS` (44 bases); **gemini** none; **copilot** `help config`, ids only, efforts curated; **antigravity** `agy models`, ids with effort baked in; **codex** `model/list`, efforts read, but `isDefault` / `defaultReasoningEffort` / speed tiers ignored; **fx**, **opencode** fully dynamic.

`gemini`, `agy` and `copilot` are **not installed on this machine**, so their probes can only be built from docs and stub fixtures, not live-verified here.

evidence.label: claude discovery today

options.label: Claude Code: new `initialize` probe
options.description: Models + per-model efforts (≥ 2.1.49).
options.consequence: Biggest win: claude is the most-updated catalog. Needs the id mapping below.

options.label: Cursor: structured base + effort + fast discovery
options.description: Strategy decided in its own question below.
options.consequence: Hardest; retires the cursor normalization-migration pattern.

options.label: Gemini: `gemini models -o json` on ≥ 0.67
options.description: Ids and labels; no efforts exist for gemini anyway.
options.consequence: Built from docs + a stub; not live-verifiable here.

options.label: Codex: also read `isDefault` / `defaultReasoningEffort`
options.description: Fields `model/list` already returns.
options.consequence: Small; only matters if defaults follow the CLI (see Defaults).

options.label: Copilot: try its ACP server for models + efforts
options.description: Copilot's ACP server is public preview; whether it exposes model/effort config options is unverified.
options.consequence: Spike at build time on a machine with copilot; falls back to today's `help config` probe.

options.label: Antigravity: no new source
options.description: `agy models` already lists ids with effort baked in.
options.consequence: Only the curated-table policy (next question) applies.

recommendation.reason: Covers every kind with a known source. Copilot ACP is unverified and copilot isn't installed here, so it would ship untested; better as its own spike.

questions.title: What happens to the hand-curated model tables (`AGENT_OPTIONS`, `MODEL_EFFORT_SUPPORT`, `CLAUDE_MODEL_FLAG`, `CURSOR_MODEL_SPECS`…)?
questions.why: Decides whether a new model release still needs a PR, and what an old or offline CLI shows.
questions.context: The tables are the only thing that keeps old CLIs working: claude < 2.1.49 reports no efforts, gemini < 0.67 reports nothing, a logged-out or offline harness reports nothing. Each table is listed with file:line in the investigation §1.2.

options.label: Keep them, frozen: fallback + optional label/hint overlay
options.description: Existing rows stay as the old/offline-CLI fallback and as overrides for copy discovery can't give (pricing, "2x usage"). **Policy: a new model never needs a new row**; a row is added only to override a label or hint.
options.consequence: No deletion risk; per-release PRs stop. The tables slowly go stale, which is fine for a fallback.

options.label: Shrink to a floor
options.description: Prune each kind to its default + one or two known-good rows.
options.consequence: Old CLIs see fewer models; tests pinning curated content need rewriting.

options.label: Delete where discovery is reliable
options.description: Remove claude/codex/cursor/gemini curated rows.
options.consequence: Old or offline CLIs show an empty picker (only the default). Breaks the "still support older versions" goal.

recommendation.reason: It is the only option that keeps old CLIs at today's behavior, and it still ends the per-release PRs.

sections.title: Claude Code: ids and account scoping
sections.intro: Claude reports ids agetor doesn't use. These answers decide whether stored data has to move.

questions.title: How do claude's CLI ids map onto agetor's model ids?
questions.why: Picks between a pure mapping rule, mixed ids, or a migration of stored task/profile/preference data.
questions.context:
Claude reports `value: "opus"` → `resolvedModel: "claude-opus-5-5"` for the current release of each family, and full ids for older ones (`claude-opus-5`, `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, dated). Agetor stores `opus-5.5`, `haiku-4.5` in `tasks.model`, `agent_profiles`, `lastModel:claude-code`, bundles and frozen pipeline/profile snapshots, and translates through `CLAUDE_MODEL_FLAG`.

A rule covers every row seen today: strip `claude-`, strip a trailing `-YYYYMMDD`, turn the last `-N-M` into `-N.M` (`claude-opus-5-5` → `opus-5.5`, `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` → `haiku-4.5`, `claude-opus-5` → `opus-5`). The reverse rule builds the `--model` argument, so `CLAUDE_MODEL_FLAG` becomes derivable.

options.label: Keep friendly ids; derive them from CLI ids by rule
options.description: Aliases resolve through `resolvedModel`; the CLI's `default` row is dropped. `CLAUDE_MODEL_FLAG` stays only as an exception list for ids the rule can't derive.
options.consequence: No stored-data migration; one id per model; a new `claude-opus-6` shows up as `opus-6` with no agetor change.
options.preview:
claude-opus-5-5            -> opus-5.5
claude-haiku-4-5-20251001  -> haiku-4.5
claude-opus-6 (future)     -> opus-6
opus (alias)               -> resolvedModel -> opus-5.5
default                    -> dropped

options.label: Use the CLI's own ids for new models only
options.description: Existing rows keep friendly ids; a new model appears as `claude-opus-6`.
options.consequence: No migration, but the picker and stored data mix two id styles forever.

options.label: Switch everything to CLI ids, with a data migration
options.description: Rewrite `tasks.model`, profiles, preferences; frozen snapshots and exported bundles can't be rewritten.
options.consequence: One-way door: a migration plus a compatibility path for old bundles/snapshots anyway.

recommendation.reason: The rule covers all 14 live rows, needs no migration, and keeps one id per model.

questions.title: Should the picker also offer auto-tracking "latest" rows (e.g. **Opus (latest)**) that follow each family's newest release?
questions.why: Decides whether a task's model can change under it when claude ships a new release.
questions.context: Claude's aliases (`opus`, `sonnet`, `fable`, `haiku`) always resolve to the family's current release. A task stored as `opus` would run Opus 6 the day claude ships it, with no agetor change and no migration. The cost: the same task can run on a different model from one turn to the next, and the run history wouldn't show which.

options.label: No alias rows
options.description: Only versioned rows; new versions appear through discovery.
options.consequence: A task keeps the model it was created with.

options.label: Add alias rows above the versioned ones
options.description: `Opus (latest)` etc., stored as the alias id and passed verbatim.
options.consequence: One more row per family; needs resolved-model display in the run panel.

options.label: Alias rows replace each family's current row
options.description: `Opus 5.5` becomes `Opus (latest)`; older versions stay pinned.
options.consequence: Existing `opus-5.5` tasks need a decision too: stay pinned, or become `opus`.

recommendation.reason: Discovery already makes new versions appear automatically; silent model changes inside a task are a new behavior worth its own decision.

questions.title: Claude's list has no Mythos rows. Should curated rows the CLI doesn't list be hidden?
questions.why: Decides whether claude joins the catalog-scoped kinds (like fx/opencode) and whether it's probed once or per account.
questions.context: **Contradiction.** The investigation assumed the list is account-scoped because Mythos is missing on your account (Claude Ultra). But `claudeModelPickerFamily`'s own comment says "claude's picker has no Mythos row of any kind", so the CLI may never list Mythos for anyone, even when `--model claude-mythos-5-2` runs. If agetor hides unlisted curated rows, Mythos would vanish for every account. Note also the fx precedent: fx is scoped because premium ids failed at run time for accounts without them.

evidence.label: picker comment
evidence.code:
* `mythos-5.1` and `mythos-5` all have no picker row
 * at all — claude's picker has no Mythos row of any kind. An unknown/future

evidence.label: the scoped kinds today
evidence.code: export const CATALOG_SCOPED_KINDS: ReadonlySet<AgentKind> = new Set<AgentKind>(["fx", "opencode"]);

options.label: Unscoped, one probe per kind
options.description: Curated rows always show (Mythos stays); discovered models are added; one probe for the default claude config.
options.consequence: Mythos stays offered to accounts that may not run it (today's behavior).

options.label: Unscoped, but probed per harness account
options.description: As above, but each claude harness (stack account, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`) gets its own probe and effort sets.
options.consequence: ~1.7 s per account per refresh; catches per-account differences in efforts and new models.

options.label: Scoped per harness: hide curated rows the account doesn't list
options.description: Like fx.
options.consequence: Mythos disappears for everyone unless the CLI lists it.

recommendation.reason: Keeps Mythos reachable, and per-account probing costs little while matching how harness stacks already treat fx/codex/opencode.

sections.title: Defaults, efforts and ordering
sections.intro: How discovered data turns into what the picker shows and what reaches the CLI.

questions.title: Default model and default effort: who picks them once discovery exists?
questions.why: Decides whether a new release changes agetor's default with no PR, and whether `DEFAULT_MODEL` keeps its per-release edits.
questions.context: Codex reports `isDefault` (gpt-6.1-sol) and `defaultReasoningEffort`; claude reports `default` → `claude-opus-5-5`. The repo departs from the CLI default on purpose in several places: fx deepseek, gemini not `auto`, cursor grok-4.7 instead of cursor's composer-2.5, copilot `auto`, each with an owner decision in a comment.

evidence.label: DEFAULT_MODEL is an owner pick with history

options.label: Owner pick stays; the CLI's default is the fallback
options.description: `DEFAULT_MODEL`/`DEFAULT_EFFORT` win. The CLI-reported default is used only when the owner pick is missing from a non-empty discovered catalog (retired model, account without it), and the CLI's per-model default effort when the owner's effort isn't in that model's ladder.
options.consequence: Moving the default to a new release is still a one-line PR, by choice.

options.label: Follow the CLI's default wherever it reports one
options.description: Owner overrides only where a deliberate departure exists (fx, cursor, copilot, gemini).
options.consequence: claude/codex defaults move with each CLI release, with no agetor change.

options.label: Owner pick only (today)
options.description: Ignore the CLI's default.
options.consequence: A retired default model stays the default until someone edits the table.

recommendation.reason: Keeps the deliberate cost/quality picks, and still fixes the retired-default case without a PR.

questions.title: A CLI reports an effort level agetor doesn't know (e.g. cursor `extra-high`, a future codex tier). What happens?
questions.why: Decides whether a new effort level needs a PR, and how much unvetted text reaches a CLI flag or env var.
questions.context: `EFFORT_OPTIONS` is a closed set of 9 ids, and `supportedEfforts` filters discovered levels through it. At spawn, claude's `CLAUDE_EFFORT_VALUES` drops anything outside 5 ids. When codex added `ultra` (#210), that took a PR. OpenCode already synthesizes rows for unknown variants (`{id, label: id}`) and passes them through.

evidence.label: discovered efforts are filtered to the closed set
claude drops unknown ids at spawn

options.label: Synthesize a row and pass it through
options.description: Label from the CLI when it gives one, else the id title-cased; sorted into the ladder where known. At spawn the value must be in that model's discovered set **and** match `^[a-z0-9_-]{1,32}$`.
options.consequence: New levels need no PR; the spawn check keeps it from being an injection path.

options.label: Keep the closed set
options.description: Unknown levels are dropped until someone adds them.
options.consequence: A new effort level still costs a release.

recommendation.reason: Same contract OpenCode already ships, and the per-model discovered-set check bounds what reaches the CLI.

questions.title: Where do discovered models land in the picker, and whose label do they show?
questions.why: With today's merge (curated rows first, discovered extras appended), a new **Opus 6** lands at the bottom, below Haiku 4.5.
questions.context: `mergeModelOptions` rule 4 (unscoped kinds): every curated row first, then discovered-only ids appended in discovered order, labeled `m.label ?? m.id`. Claude's list is newest-first by family (Opus, Fable, Sonnet, Haiku, then older versions). Labels: claude/codex/fx/gemini report clean display names; cursor's carry literal zero-width spaces and need sanitizing either way.

evidence.label: merge rule 4
evidence.code:
* 4. `scoped === false` and `discovered` is non-empty → every curated row
 *    (rule 1 still gates `catalogOnly` ones), followed by discovered-only
 *    ids the same way as rule 3. This is the unchanged behavior the
 *    NewTaskForm/RunPanel merge sites had before per-kind scoping existed.

options.label: CLI order wins; curated-only rows follow
options.description: When discovery is non-empty: discovered rows in the CLI's order, each carrying the curated label/hint if one exists, else the CLI's display name (and description as hint); curated rows the CLI didn't list (Mythos) come after, in curated order. Discovery empty → today's curated order.
options.consequence: New models appear where the CLI puts them (top, for claude). The order of existing rows changes for claude/codex/gemini.

options.label: Keep curated first, discovered appended (today)
options.consequence: New models sit at the bottom until someone adds a curated row, which brings back the per-release PR.

options.label: Group by family, newest version first
options.description: Agetor sorts by parsed family + version.
options.consequence: Needs a family/version parser per kind; brittle for cursor and fx's 136 ids.

recommendation.reason: The CLI's order already puts the current release first, and it's the only option that needs no curated row for a good position.

questions.title: Cursor: where do its model families, effort levels and fast variants come from?
questions.why: Cursor is the hardest kind, and 8 of the 11 id-normalization migrations are cursor's.
questions.context:
Three sources, all spiked on cursor-agent 2026.10.22:

- **Flat list** (`cursor-agent models`): 282 `id - Label` lines, side-effect free, ~1–3 s. Grammar is irregular: `grok-4.7-high-fast`, `claude-4.6-sonnet-medium-thinking`, a bare base id that is the default variant, `cursor-grok-4.5-*` vs ACP base `grok-4.5`.
- **ACP `session/new`**: 48 base models; no effort info.
- **ACP parameterized picker**: exact per-model effort/fast/context params, but **52 s for all 48**, and each `set_config_option` **writes your `~/.cursor/cli-config.json`** (the spike changed your default model; it was restored).

evidence.label: flat list sample (S4)
evidence.code:
grok-4.7-high - Grok 4.7  High
grok-4.7-high-fast - Grok 4.7  High Fast
claude-4.6-sonnet-medium - Claude Sonnet 4.6 1M
claude-4.6-sonnet-medium-thinking - Claude Sonnet 4.6 1M Thinking

options.label: Parse the flat list into base + effort + fast
options.description: Known effort/fast suffixes are peeled off the id; anything that doesn't parse stays a plain row with no effort picker. `CURSOR_MODEL_SPECS` stays as a frozen overlay for bases it already knows, and wins where both exist.
options.consequence: Side-effect free, one call. Normalization moves to read time, so no more cursor migrations. An odd new suffix shows as an extra row until the parser learns it.

options.label: ACP `session/new` for the base list, flat list for variants
options.description: Bases come from cursor's own grouping; variants are matched to bases by prefix.
options.consequence: More exact base list, two probes, and an ACP session per refresh (assumed to write nothing, unverified).

options.label: ACP parameterized enumeration
options.description: Exact, but needs an isolated cursor config that keeps your login (unproven).
options.consequence: 52 s per refresh and a real risk of rewriting your cursor defaults.

options.label: Keep `CURSOR_MODEL_SPECS` as the source
options.description: Only stop writing migrations; new bases still need a spec row.
options.consequence: Cursor stays per-release.

recommendation.reason: The only exact source mutates your config and takes 52 s; the flat list is safe and the specs overlay covers today's bases exactly.

questions.title: Claude (`supportsFastMode`) and codex (`fast` service tier) report speed tiers. Do they belong in this change?
questions.why: In scope means a new Speed picker and a new spawn flag for two harnesses, not just discovery.
questions.context: Speed exists today only for cursor and fx. Adding it for claude/codex needs new driver work (how claude's fast mode is switched per run is unverified) plus a picker, a stored field path and tests. Discovering the flag alone, without using it, adds nothing visible.

options.label: Out of scope: separate ticket
options.description: This change stays models + efforts; parsers keep the flag so the follow-up has it.
options.consequence: Smaller change; Speed for claude/codex is its own feature.

options.label: In this change
options.consequence: Adds driver spikes for claude fast mode and codex service tier, a Speed picker for two more kinds, and e2e coverage.

recommendation.reason: The task is models and efforts; Speed on claude/codex is a new user-facing feature with its own unknowns.

questions.title: Retire the per-model minimum-CLI-version table (`MODEL_MIN_CLI_VERSION`) where discovery is authoritative?
questions.why: Every new codex/copilot model adds a floor row today; this is one of the per-release edits.
questions.context: The codex catalog is client-version-gated: a CLI too old for a model simply doesn't list it. So "the model is missing from a non-empty discovered catalog" says the same thing as the floor, without a table. Copilot's `help config` lists the ids its binary knows, which is the same signal. The floor also runs at harness-stack failover (`harness-failover.ts:253`).

evidence.code:
export const MODEL_MIN_CLI_VERSION: Partial<Record<AgentKind, Record<string, string>>> = {
  codex: {
    "gpt-6.1-sol": "0.159.0",
    "gpt-6.1-terra": "0.159.0",
    "gpt-6-sol": "0.155.0",
    "gpt-6-luna": "0.155.0",
    "gpt-6-astra": "0.153.0",
    "gpt-6-astra-aeon": "0.153.0",

options.label: Discovery check first; the table becomes a frozen fallback
options.description: Pre-flight and failover refuse a model missing from a non-empty authoritative catalog (codex, copilot) with an "upgrade the CLI" message; the table is used only when discovery is empty and gets no new rows.
options.consequence: No more floor rows per release; old entries keep protecting offline/failed-probe starts.

options.label: Delete the table
options.consequence: A failed probe means no pre-flight at all; old CLIs hit the misleading 400 again.

options.label: Keep as is
options.consequence: Still a per-release edit for codex and copilot.

recommendation.reason: Ends the per-release edit and keeps the safety net for the failed-probe case.

questions.title: Should the last discovered catalog survive a restart?
questions.why: Without it, a cold or offline start shows curated-only rows until the first probe lands, so a task on a discovered-only model shows as "unlisted" for a while.
questions.context: The cache is in-memory today (`agent-discovery.ts:1201`, `cache` and `harnessCache`). The generic `preferences` key-value table can hold JSON with no migration (the `theme` preference does the same). A dedicated table needs a migration, which can't be undone on users' databases.

options.label: Persist in the `preferences` table, no migration
options.description: One key per kind/harness (`modelCatalog:<id>`), storing the catalog, the CLI version it came from and a timestamp. Used until a fresh probe replaces it; dropped when the CLI version changes. Only the parsed models are stored (never claude's account/email fields).
options.consequence: Discovered rows survive restarts and offline starts; no schema change.

options.label: A new table (migration)
options.consequence: One-way schema change for a cache.

options.label: Don't persist (today)
options.consequence: Discovered-only models flicker to "unlisted" after every restart until the probe lands (~2–8 s).

recommendation.reason: Makes "dynamic" rows stable across restarts with no migration and an easy rollback.

sections.title: Confirm or override
sections.intro: Defaults I'd bet on. Confirm with one click, or override with what it should be.

questions.title: Pre-existing bug: curated Opus 4.6 offers `xhigh`, which claude says it doesn't support

recommendation.value: Fix the curated row in this change (drop `xhigh` from `opus-4.6`), so old CLIs without discovery stop offering it too. A stored `xhigh` on existing tasks is kept (`retainableEfforts`), never PATCHed away.
recommendation.reason: Spike S1d; discovery alone would fix it only on claude ≥ 2.1.49.

questions.title: Claude probe isolation and privacy

recommendation.value: Spawn through `coreSpawn` with `--strict-mcp-config` (no MCP servers), `disableAllHooks`, `--no-session-persistence`, an empty cwd under the data dir, the harness's `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, a 10 s timeout. Parse only `models[]`; never log or store the raw response (it carries the account email and org). If build-time checks show MCP servers or hooks still start, claude stays curated and that's reported back.
recommendation.reason: MCP start-up at `initialize` is unverified (investigation assumption 1).

questions.title: When the new probes run

recommendation.value: Same scheduler and triggers as today's probes: boot, harness status change, harness CRUD, manual refresh, and the 15-minute sweep. No new route or SSE stream; reuse `agent_models_changed`.
recommendation.reason: Claude costs ~1.7 s per account; the cadence already works for codex/fx/opencode.

questions.title: A discovered model with no reported efforts and no curated row

recommendation.value: Today's fallback stays: the default model's ladder for claude (< 2.1.49) and copilot, no effort picker for gemini, antigravity and unparsed cursor rows. Haiku 4.5's curated "no effort" stays authoritative.
recommendation.reason: It is what old CLIs get today; changing it is a separate decision.

questions.title: Cursor driver keeps flat variant ids

recommendation.value: The cursor driver keeps passing flat variant ids (`grok-4.7-high-fast`), not the bracket form `base[effort=…,fast=…]`.
recommendation.reason: Fleet evidence (JubarteAI 421157fb) found bracket values rejected for several models, and each test is a paid request.

questions.title: Pre-existing: agetor's cursor runs may change your interactive cursor default

recommendation.value: Check once during the build (compare `~/.cursor/cli-config.json` before and after a run). If agetor runs do change it, record that as a separate ticket; this change only makes sure the new discovery never writes it.
recommendation.reason: It is pre-existing driver behavior (`cursor-acp.ts:789`), not part of discovery.

questions.title: Copilot and antigravity keep their current probes

recommendation.value: Copilot keeps `help config` (ids) with curated efforts, and antigravity keeps `agy models`. The curated-table policy above applies to both. A copilot ACP probe becomes its own spike, unless you ticked it under Scope.
recommendation.reason: Neither is installed here, so nothing new could be live-verified.

questions.title: Bundles, `agetor add` and the TUI

recommendation.value: Bundle import's "unknown model" warning, `agetor add --model/--effort` validation and the TUI use curated ∪ discovered from the core (`GET /agent-models`). Third-party labels and ids printed by the CLI/TUI go through `escapeFreeText` / `escapeControlChars`.
recommendation.reason: Otherwise a discovered model is selectable in the app but rejected by the CLI.

questions.title: Acceptance bar and tests

recommendation.value: Done means: a stub claude reporting a new `claude-opus-6` with its own effort ladder makes **Opus 6** appear in the New Task picker, the task editor and `agetor add`, with that ladder and no agetor change; an old/failed probe gives today's curated picker. Tests: a parser unit test per probe with redacted spike fixtures; a cross-kind invariant that no merged picker has two rows for the same CLI model or the same label (the S2 bug); `supportedEfforts` with unknown levels; one Playwright e2e on the stub claude, extending the fx stub-bin seam.
recommendation.reason: These pin the user-visible promise and the duplication bug no test catches today.

questions.title: Docs

recommendation.value: Update `harnesses.md` (the add-a-model / add-a-kind checklist: a new model needs no PR unless it wants a label/hint override), each touched `harness-<kind>.md`, and CLAUDE.md's "Agent kinds at a glance" probe column. Copy the goal into `docs/plans/dynamic-model-catalog.md` with the plan.
recommendation.reason: Repo rule: a behavior change updates its subsystem doc in the same change.
